findings.gate: Combat 2: Positions and movement remain legible

draft_evidence.quote: Meridian took the center at the horn, all seven of them, at a run.

comparison_evidence.quote: The clipboard had eight names on it... Vey... Holt... Vale... Bell... Shah... Kim... Navarro... Mercer.

findings.consequence: A listener can momentarily infer an unexplained absent teammate at the start of the most spatially complex round, although all eight appear in the subsequent action.
findings.repair_target: State the correct participant count or explicitly identify which roster member is not part of the center rush.

draft_evidence.quote: Nessa reached the zone behind him and said, "Track, two," and Anton let go on one.

comparison_evidence.quote: When I do, you'll get three words. Where, how many, how sure. North, two, high. If I say low, I'm guessing.

findings.consequence: The chapter establishes a precise fatigue-safe three-word protocol, then breaks it during its intended payoff, leaving the confidence state unknowable and weakening the receipt for Nessa's competence under cost.
findings.repair_target: Make the late call follow the established three-part order, or clearly establish that 'Track, two' is a different countdown instruction rather than a sensory contact call.

concerns: The skipped sibling-message number thirty-nine may sound like a missing section in audio, but the packet does not establish that every number must appear, so this remains a concern rather than a finding.

The final preparation/celebration/debrief reiterates the distributed-team insight after the rounds have already demonstrated it; selective trimming there is the safest route under the remaining 205-word overage.

The source's early east-gate opening and Nobel respawn are altered, but the frozen ledgers and packet lock the durable outcome, score, eliminations, token state, and placement rather than those exact transient tactics; no contradiction is proven.
strengths: The tape-floor rehearsal turns strategy into embodied ensemble competence and makes later reversals feel earned.
Round Two has especially clear geography, load accounting, handoffs, injury persistence, and role differentiation.
Kade's elimination is caused by an established personal failure mode, while Mara's refusal to respawn him supplies both tactical causality and emotional cost.
Nessa's recovery scene converts sensory overload into team accommodation without sentimentalizing or diminishing her competence.
The unspent token, Eli's west-port play, and Mara's better call convincingly prove that Kade empowers a system capable of improving without him.
The closing Mara exchange preserves the chapter's relationship turn and ends on changed pressure toward the final.
